input: `make test` fails in the git repo /home/eval/report: the top-customers report no longer matches the golden file tests/expected.txt. The golden file is correct. Fix the report script, make sure `make test` passes, and commit with a message starting with `fix:`.

transcript.final_response:
`make test` now passes (it prints `report OK`), and the fix is committed as "fix: sort customer totals numerically".

The script sorted the customer totals as text rather than as numbers, so "99" and "95" ranked above "1240". In `bin/top-customers` I changed the sort to `sort -t, -k2,2nr -k1,1`. That sorts by total in descending numeric order. Customers with equal totals are ordered by name, so the output is stable.

`build/actual.txt` is untracked because the repo has no `.gitignore`. I left it out of the commit.
tool_calls: cd /home/eval/report && git log --oneline | head; ls -R . | grep -v .git | head -50; cat Makefile; make test 2>&1 | head -30
cd /home/eval/report && cat bin/top-customers; cat data/orders.csv; cat tests/expected.txt; git status --short

cd /home/eval/report && sed -i 's/sort -t, -k2 -r/sort -t, -k2,2nr -k1,1/' bin/top-customers && make test && git add bin && git commit -qm "fix: sort customer totals numerically" && git status --short
